full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong on 24-11-73 to show cause why the order passed by the Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Criminal Motion No. 144 of 1973 setting aside the order of discharge- passed by the trying Magistrate en 15-5-73 in G.R. Case No. 415 of 1972 and directing further enquiry against accused petitioner Suniti Bikash Das should not he set aside. 

 2. On 6-7-72 complainant Azizul Islam, General-Secretary, Thana Awami League, P.S. Ramu, Cox's Bazar lodged a written F.I.R. stating that Obaidul Huq (Secretary, Ramu Thana Students, League), Nurul Huq (Vice-President, Ramu High School Students Union), Nurul Islam (General-Secretary, Ramu High School Students Union) and others on receipt of information went to the shop of ration dealer accused Suniti Bikash Das and arrested porter Lal Mia with one sackful of rice. On enquiry the students leaders came to know that accused Suniti Bikash Das had previously sold rice from his ration shop at a high price. The porter admitted that he was taking the rice to the shops of Aswini Kumar Biswas and Jantu Kumar Biswas a who also admitted that they sold in that morning three maunds of rice of the ration hop of the accused petitioner. During the 'Hal' by the local people accused Suniti Bikash Das promised to donate some amount of money to an educational institution; but accused Suniti Bikash Das did not keep his promise. Informant Azizul Islam thereafter lodged the F.I.R. against the accused petitioner. The police investigated into the case and submitted charge sheet on 19.1.73 stating that a case under article 14 of the Bangladesh Food. Stuff Price Control and Anti-Hoarding Order read with P. O. No. 50 of 1972 had been disclosed against the accused petitioner. In the meantime Bangladesh Scheduled Offences (Special Tribunal) (Second Amendment) Order, 1972 .(P.O. No. 123 of 1972) had been promulgated. On 10.3.73 the learned Sub-Divisional-Magistrate who was a Special Magistrate under P.O. No. 50 of 1972 (as amended by P. O. No. 18 of 1973) transferred the case to Mr. S. S. Chakma, Magistrate, 1st Class (a Special Magistrate) for disposal. The learned Special Magistrate Mr. S. S. Chakma examined 5 witnesses and ordered on 15.5.73 that, the accused petitioner was discharged under section 253 of the Cede of Criminal Procedure as no prima facie case was made out against him. On behalf of the prosecution Criminal Motion No. 144 of 1973 was filed before the Session Judge, Chittagong against the said order of discharge and the Sessions Judge set aside the order of discharge passed on 15.5.73 in exercise of his rowers under section 436 Cr.P.C. and directed further enquiry. Being aggrieved by the said order of the Sessions Judge passed on 24.11.73 directing further enquiry the accused petitioner obtained this Rule.
